newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's whites stage bloody protest against ANC.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's whites stage bloody protest against ANC.

text.p: White rightists staged a bloody protest outside the headquarters of the ruling African National Congress on Saturday, demanding the prosecution of ANC security guards who opened fire on a Zulu march two years ago.

Eight Zulus were shot dead outside the ANC's offices during the protest march in central Johannesburg on March 28, 1994. At least 42 other people were killed in violence surrounding that march, called in support of the Zulu monarchy.

Accusing President Nelson Mandela's government of applying selective justice, four right-wingers opened large plastic packets of fresh cow's blood and poured it ceremoniously on the spot where the eight Zulus died.
"This action is to try to draw attention to the fact that the law system in South Africa is completely skewed," a spokesman for the right-wingers, "Commandant" Willem Ratte, told Reuters.
"The people who support the ANC and South African Communist Party are getting away with mass murders, like this one which took place two years ago and nobody's been prosecuted," he said.
Police had cordoned off the 17-storey building with coils of razor wire and formed a human barricade to prevent the protesters from entering the party's headquarters. The event passed off peacefully.
Black onlookers jeered the white rightists and urinated and spat on the blood, chanting "Down with the Boere (Afrikaners), Down" and singing the ANC's praises.
The mess was later hosed away by firemen.
ANC spokesman Ronnie Mamoepa said in a terse statement afterwards:

"The protest by the right-wingers at the ANC's headquarters is a publicity stunt and was unnecessary. The ANC expressess its confidence in the ability of the attorney-general's office to investigate this (the shooting) to the best of their ability."
Inquiries are still under way into the shooting which occurred weeks before all-race elections ended white rule in South Africa. No one has been arrested.
Mandela acknowledged last year he had given the ANC's security guards the order to shoot if it became necessary to repel an attack by the Zulu marchers "even if they had to kill people".
